title: Epictetus: some things are in our control and others are not
summary: Elizabeth Carter's translation of the Enchiridion opens with that distinction.
body: The Internet Classics Archive publishes Elizabeth Carter's translation of Epictetus's Enchiridion. The first section says some things are in our control and others are not, and lists opinion, pursuit, desire, aversion, and our own actions as in our control. The modern slogan "it's not what happens to you, but how you react" is a paraphrase, not this sentence. The v1 article also attributes "the obstacle is the way" to Marcus Aurelius. That wording is a modern compression. Wikisource holds a translation of the Meditations, and this card does not pretend the slogan is a verbatim line.
